chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar, from Abu Baseer, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the one who recites from the Mushaf while he is without wudu. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem, but he should not touch the Book.'

key_terms.الْمُصْحَفِ: The physical copy of the Quran
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to recite the Quran without wudu in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between the act of recitation (tilawah) and physical contact (mass) with the Quranic text, affirming that sexual impurity (junub) does not invalidate recitation. It reflects the Shia juristic view that while wudu is recommended for reverence, it is not a strict condition for reciting from memory or the Mushaf, provided one avoids touching the physical copy directly. This ruling underscores the practical flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding ritual purity during daily Quranic engagement.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Mukhtar, from Abu Baseer who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the one who recites the Parchment and he is without an Ablution (Wudhu). Heasws said: ‘There is no problem, but he should not touch the Book (Quran)’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar from abu Basir who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about one who reads from a copy of al-Mushaf (the book) without Wudu’. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful, but one must not touch the book in such condition.’”
